scope: Proposition 1.14 (Packet representation) of the manuscript “A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions” (preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 083 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 38d5c48b4d835003), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The diagonal form X j ⟨Au,L e Qjfj, gj⟩ is a sum, with absolutely summable scalar coefficients, of averages of forms (1.33). Each form satisfies Theorem 1.13, uniformly in w, m, L, and has one common angular grid and common spatial lattices across components. The same assertion holds for m = 1 with the original positive-frequency band cutoff in place of e Q1. The sums can be obtained as limits of finite packet collections.
